title: NivKode re-tested, next release candidate chosen: 9 October update
text: NivKode remains in testing. On 9 October a newer build was re-tested in full, exactly as it would be reviewed, and an automated cross-review accepted it as our next release candidate; human review, release approval and publication are still to come. We develop NivKode in a recorded workshop: AI workers take tasks, every job, review and hand-off is recorded, and merging to the live product or publishing a release still needs a human decision. We also continue to measure open models on our own hardware, and will publish figures only alongside their evidence. Our target for the public release is 2 November 2026, and it may move if testing finds issues.

title: Corrections to our 3 October update
text: Our 3 October update used unsupported product feature and test descriptions. Those claims were withdrawn in our 6 October correction. NivKode accessibility options remain under evaluation; no accessibility assessment is claimed.

title: NivKode 0.1.0 review candidate: 6 October update
text: NivKode 0.1.0 is a review candidate. Development continues. Human review, release approval and publication are pending. Our target for the public release is 2 November 2026, and it may move if testing finds issues. The NivKode source code is licensed AGPL-3.0-only but is not public yet.

title: NivKode 0.1.0 RC8 is a review candidate
text: NivKode 0.1.0 RC8 is a review candidate and remains in testing. Release approval and publication are pending. No platform-specific test results are reported here. The launch target remains 2 November 2026 and may move if testing finds issues. We also corrected our own research records: some ratings we'd labelled as human were made by an AI model. Those results stay inconclusive, and we've tightened our rules so it can't happen again. Honest results matter more than good-looking ones.

title: NivKode 0.1.0 RC6 is ready for testing
text: Superseded by our corrections on 6 and 7 October. The product feature and test descriptions in this entry were withdrawn because they were not supported by public evidence. Some ratings in our research records were labelled as human but were made by an AI model; those results remain inconclusive.
